title: kv-cache: introduce adaptive memory rebalancer and spillover-aware eviction heuristics
author: Arielle Chen
description: Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and uncoordinated spillover have been a leading cause of OOMs and tail-latency spikes when serving long-chat workloads. This PR implements an adaptive memory rebalancer plus spillover-aware eviction heuristics to reduce fragmentation, limit disruptive paging, and prioritize compactable entries for background compaction. The change is conservatively gated behind a runtime feature flag and is rolled out as a canary on dedicated pools before global rollout. Summary of work: 1) add an AdaptiveMemoryRebalancer that periodically scans slab utilization across model contexts and adjusts per-context soft/target allocations to reduce cross-context fragmentation; 2) introduce a SpilloverAwareEvictor that augments LRU with a fragmentation score and paging cost estimate so we preferentially evict small, high-fragmentation slots and avoid evicting entries that would trigger disk/page reads for immediate reuse; 3) new background compaction worker that coalesces nearby free fragments when utilization crosses thresholds; 4) telemetry and knobs: kv.rebalancer.*, kv.evictor.*, kv.compaction.* metrics and config; 5) unit + integration tests + perf benchmarks and upgrade script for on-prem nodes. Expected impact: fewer OOMs under high-concurrency workloads, 9-15% improved throughput for mixed long/short sequences in our perf lab, and 20-40% reduction in paging events in stress tests. Rollout plan: enable on canary nodes in dedicated pool (flag: feature.kv_rebalancer=true), run 72h soak with traffic profile A/B, then progressive rollout cluster-wide with dynamic threshold tuning. Related: ENG-2211 design doc, ENG-2298 follow-up to spillover incident triage.

review_comments: Evan Brooks (review): Can you add a per-model soft cap to avoid starving large (long-seq) contexts? Also please document the expected metrics and alert thresholds. (requested changes)

Lina Gomez (review): The compaction worker might contend with latency-critical token generation. Please gate compaction to background QoS and make the compaction window configurable. (requested changes)

Author (Arielle): Compaction now runs on a low-priority worker pool; added kv.compaction.window_ms and kv.compaction.max_ops_per_cycle knobs. Added unit tests to assert compaction yields expected free-run behavior.

release_notes: Introduce AdaptiveMemoryRebalancer to reduce KV cache fragmentation and rebalance per-context allocations.
Add SpilloverAwareEvictor that combines LRU with fragmentation and paging-cost heuristics to reduce unnecessary paging and prioritize compactable evictions.
Background compaction worker to coalesce free fragments and reduce long-term fragmentation.
New telemetry: kv.rebalancer.*, kv.evictor.*, kv.compaction.* and suggested alert thresholds documented.
Performance: 9-15% throughput improvement on mixed workloads in perf lab; 20-40% fewer paging events in stress tests.
notes: This change should be monitored carefully during rollout for any regression in token latency for extremely latency-sensitive routes; knobs are exposed to tune aggressiveness. Customers on Private should run the provided migration script before enabling the feature to ensure safe slab layout transitions.
